name: A global --text prints every CLI answer as coloured text for a person
summary: The CLI answers in JSON for agents. With --text anywhere before --, the same answer prints as coloured text that names each field in words, so that a person can read it.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/nAmiQ3Vc#EMV2VjBX
changes.value: bin.ts runs the bootstrap of routing/operations first, then the command table in run.ts. The bootstrap takes --url and the global --text out of argv before routing; output to a pipe loses its colour unless --text asks for text. session.ts reads the global flags, the addressed vault and a help request, and dispatch.ts picks one route of the registry and runs it through runCommand of Command contract, saying whether an agent or a person reads the answer.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/XppR9owz#o5zkAtUT
changes.value: contract/protocol defines a command and contract/operations runs one: runCommand in runner.ts is the one call routing makes, and it passes straight on to executeCommand in execution.ts. contract/rules turns a contract into Commander parsing and the usage that help prints, and turns an answer into the text a person reads when the global --text asks for it (TASK-602): each field named in words, records with short fields as a table, a refusal said to be one, coloured where standard output shows colour. A handler learns from its context who reads the answer, so repo list and browser panes keep their own read-outs.
